claims.text: HfNbTaTiZr is a refractory high-entropy alloy system.
The initial HfNbTaTiZr state is a random solid solution.
The random solid solution has severe lattice distortion caused by atomic-size mismatch and random chemical distribution.
The random solid solution has high phonon-scattering rates and consequently low lattice thermal conductivity.
Controlled annealing or Monte Carlo treatment promotes HfTi and TiZr short-range-order clusters in HfNbTaTiZr.
Annealing can produce ordered B2-like structures in the treated alloy.
A temperature range of 800–1200 K is sufficient for SRO-forming diffusion while remaining below the melting point.
HfTi and TiZr clusters undergo a percolative transition into a connected network of B2-like domains.
B2-like ordering reduces the variance of local atomic environments and the global lattice distortion relative to the random solid solution.
Point-defect phonon scattering in random alloys follows a rate proportional to ω^4Γ, with Γ dependent on mass and size variance.
Chemical ordering lowers the effective scattering parameter Γ for high-frequency phonons by reducing local mass and size disorder within ordered domains.
Percolated ordered domains create continuous phonon-transport channels with lower scattering rates than the random matrix.
Reduced point-defect scattering and phonon channeling increase phonon mean free paths and lattice thermal conductivity.
The lattice thermal conductivity of the SRO or percolated state will be 10–30% higher than that of the random solid solution.
Lattice thermal conductivity will increase or vary non-monotonically with SRO and peak near the percolation threshold.
The ordered state will exhibit sharper, less broadened high-frequency phonon-DOS features than the random solid solution.
A conductivity increase requires a connected, low-distortion B2-like network; isolated or incoherent precipitates will instead reduce conductivity through interface scattering.
The proposed conductivity enhancement is limited to the high-frequency phonon regime.
